newsitem.title: DUBAI: Yemeni mediators in talks to free French diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni mediators in talks to free French diplomat.

text.p: Yemeni mediators on Monday negotiated with tribesmen who recaptured a French diplomat shortly after releasing him, officials said.
"Talks are still continuing and...we hope a good result will come out soon," one official told Reuters by telephone from the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
Security forces were ringing the village where most of the kidnappers were staying, another official said.
The officials declined to give more details on the kidnapping, seen as an embarrassment to Yemeni authorities.

Members of the al-Toaiman tribe recaptured the French diplomat hours after freeing him late on Saturday from six days of captivity to press grievances against the government, a French Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Sunday in Paris.

The diplomat, identified by local authorities as a first secretary at the Sanaa embassy, and his Yemeni escort, were abducted on their way to the capital Sanaa on Saturday night from the province of Marib where he was being held.
The diplomat, whom the ministry has declined to identify, was first seized last Monday as he drove his car in Sanaa.

The al-Toaiman tribesmen released him to three prominent tribal chiefs who were mediating on behalf of the government after they dropped their demands and asked for a guarantee that they would not be prosecuted if they released their hostage.
Details of the arrangements they made were not made public.
But officials believed the second abduction might have been prompted by a strongly worded Interior Ministry statement late on Saturday which vowed to punish the abductors.
The tribe wants government compensation for losses to homes, farms, water pumps and wells by floods that killed 65 people in June. It also wants more jobs and settlement of a land dispute.

At least two diplomats, a Saudi ambassador and an American, have been among foreigners and tourists kidnapped in recent years and used as bargaining chips by Yemeni tribesmen pressing mostly non-political grievances against the government.
